solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Eccentric wore drab clothes

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of the next two words are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone peculiar is dressed in dull, shabby garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' looks like a noun for the wearer, but it is the anagram signal working on WORE DRAB; 'clothes' is a noun here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's whole collection of garments is called their wardrobe, by extension from the cupboard that holds them.

clue.text: Filmmaker, more passionate

definitions.meaning: Billy ..., the Austrian-born Hollywood director of Some Like It Hot
comparative of wild in its sense of fiercely emotional or unrestrained

explanation.surface: A movie director described as more fiery than another.
explanation.definitionFit: Billy Wilder was a famous film director; and the comparative adjective of 'wild' means more unrestrained or ardent.

clue.text: Change bottom line

parts.note: the rear is the backside or bottom
a range is a line or row, as of mountains

explanation.surface: An instruction to alter the lowest row of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange something is to alter its order, a straightforward synonym for changing it.

clue.text: Wash resin off

indicators.note: off means wrong or not right, so the letters of the sticky word are disturbed

explanation.surface: Instructions for cleaning sticky resin away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' reads as removing the resin, but it signals rearranging the five letters of RESIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse is to wash lightly with clean water, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Blessing given by one disciple at foot of mountain

indicators.note: in a down clue, being at the foot of something means coming below it, so these pieces follow the mountain

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
the Roman numeral for one is I
son can mean a follower or disciple, as a spiritual son of a teacher

explanation.surface: A follower of a holy man bestows a blessing at the bottom of a mountain, like the Sermon on the Mount.
explanation.walkthrough: BEN is the Scottish mountain word; 'at foot of' places I and SON below it in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Benison is an old literary word for a blessing or benediction.

clue.text: Monstrous woman therefore capsized vessel

indicators.note: a capsized boat is upside down, so the Latin word is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore
SS stands for steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: A fearsome woman, and so a boat has overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogress is a female ogre, a monstrous giantess of fairy tales.

clue.text: Place in TV studio for the rest of the guests?

definitions.text: Place in TV studio for the rest of the guests?

parts.words: Place in TV studio for the rest of the guests?
parts.note: 'rest' looks like 'the remaining guests', but means relaxation: the lounge where performers wait and unwind before going on air

explanation.surface: A query about where the remaining guests on a TV show are put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the rest of the guests' seems to mean the others, but it means where guests take their rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The waiting lounge for performers in a theatre or broadcast studio is traditionally called by this name.

clue.text: Sly person lacking wife's support

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the letter for wife is removed

parts.note: a weasel is a sly, devious person
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A crafty character without his wife's backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wife's support' looks like one phrase, but the possessive splits: the wife's W is dropped from WEASEL, leaving 'support' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand that holds up a painter's canvas, so it is a kind of support.

clue.text: Dark finish to bowler, old hat

parts.note: sombre means dark or gloomy

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its last letter, taken here from bowler

explanation.surface: A dark ending for a bowler, an old hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' and 'hat' together suggest a bowler hat, but 'bowler' just supplies its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a wide-brimmed Mexican hat.

clue.text: Lecturer getting paid for knowledge

parts.note: earning means receiving pay for work

explanation.surface: An academic is paid for what they know.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning, as a noun, means knowledge acquired through study, a scholar's erudition.

clue.text: Discarded stuff from plane, almost identical

parts.note: a jet is an aeroplane

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: same means identical

explanation.surface: Rubbish thrown from an aircraft looks nearly the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is goods thrown overboard from a ship to lighten it, hence discarded material.

clue.text: Elegant young woman docked

indicators.note: docked means having its tail cut short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: chick is slang for a young woman

explanation.surface: A stylish young woman whose boat has come into port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' suggests a ship, but it means cut short like a dog's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and fashionable, a synonym for elegant.

clue.text: Ghostly English lake

parts.note: Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A haunted English lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and frightening in a supernatural way, close in sense to spooky.

clue.text: Small children worried Oskar, hero of film

indicators.note: worried can mean shaken about, as a dog worries a bone, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Little ones fretted about Oskar, the hero of a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' reads as describing the children's mood, but here it is the anagram signal, as a dog worries a bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Oskar Schindler, the industrialist who saved Jews in wartime, is the hero of Spielberg's film Schindler's List.

clue.text: Trade Union alliance across the south

indicators.note: across means spanning or stretched over, so the alliance word goes round the compass letter

parts.note: a union is an alliance

explanation.surface: A labour body forming a coalition spanning the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Unison is the largest public-sector trade union in the UK.

clue.text: Choice piece about the Parisian

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the piece word goes around the French article

parts.note: a section is a piece or part
le is French for the, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A tasty morsel concerning the man from Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A selection is a choice, either the act of choosing or a range chosen from.

clue.text: Cowherd could make a soup

indicators.note: could make says the letters of the herdsman can be formed into something new

explanation.surface: A cattle herder might be able to cook up a soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Chowder is a thick soup, typically of clams or fish, from New England.

clue.text: Challenged wicked adventurer

parts.note: dared means challenged someone to do something
evil means wicked

explanation.surface: A villainous thrill-seeker who was challenged.
explanation.definitionFit: A daredevil is a reckless person who seeks out dangerous exploits, an adventurer.

clue.text: Magical feeling beginning around twilight, mostly

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the beginning word encloses the rest

parts.note: start means beginning

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: dusk is twilight

explanation.surface: An enchanted mood starting as the evening gets dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims only the twilight word, which then sits inside the beginning word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardust is a dreamy, romantic or magical quality, as in a sprinkling of glamour.

clue.text: Report is about right support for climbers

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the two words go round the letter for right

parts.note: to tell is to report

explanation.surface: A report about the right equipment for mountaineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbers' suggests mountaineers, but means climbing plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice framework on which climbing plants are trained to grow.

clue.text: Fraudulent operation in tennis camp

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the run of words that follows, across the word gap

explanation.surface: A swindle being run at a tennis training camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a dishonest scheme, a con or swindle.

clue.text: Look up to one in weird dream

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the jumbled letters
weird means strange, so the letters of dream are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Gazing up at someone in a strange dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weird' turns DREAM into ADMRE, and 'in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to respect and esteem them, the idiom 'look up to'.

clue.text: Mean to declare seniority

parts.note: to aver is to declare or assert
age can mean seniority, being older

explanation.surface: Intending to announce one's senior status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb (intend), but it is the noun, a statistical middle value.
explanation.definitionFit: The arithmetic mean is the average: the sum divided by the count.

clue.text: US actor and British writer broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the airwaves, so the clue wants what sounds like the writer's name

parts.note: H G Wells, the British author of The War of the Worlds

explanation.surface: An American actor and an English author on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Orson Welles famously broadcast a radio version of Wells's The War of the Worlds.
explanation.definitionFit: Orson Welles was the American actor and director of Citizen Kane.

clue.text: Here pace altered, round middle of tight supplemetary heat

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the rearranged letters enclose the picked letter
altered means changed, so the letters of the two words are rearranged
the middle of a five-letter word is its third letter

explanation.surface: Here the pace has changed, a round in the middle of a tight extra race.
explanation.walkthrough: HERE PACE is rearranged to REPEC_HAGE around G, the centre of 'tight'. 'supplemetary' is the clue's own misspelling of supplementary.
explanation.definitionFit: A repechage is an extra qualifying race in rowing or cycling giving losers a second chance.

clue.text: Move stealthily in bow (front of liner)

parts.note: the prow is the bow of a ship

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, here taken from liner

explanation.surface: Creeping about in the bow of an ocean liner.
explanation.definitionFit: To prowl is to move about quietly and stealthily, as a predator does.

clue.text: Chaplain in flat connected with religious education

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat or home
RE is religious education, a British school subject

explanation.surface: A clergyman living in an apartment, linked with scripture classes.
explanation.definitionFit: A padre is a military chaplain, from the Spanish and Italian word for father.

clue.text: A grass, an informant originally arrested by policeman

indicators.note: being arrested by means held inside, so the police abbreviation goes round the other letters

parts.note: PC is a police constable

indicators.note: originally means at first, so the first letter of informant is taken

explanation.surface: A police officer nicks a snitch and an informer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' looks like British slang for an informer, matching 'informant', but it is the plant. PC holds AN plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic grass is a genus of grasses (Panicum), so the word can name a grass.

clue.text: More would have us believe this is the perfect place

definitions.text: More would have us believe this is the perfect place

parts.words: More would have us believe this is the perfect place
parts.note: More is Sir Thomas More, whose 1516 book describes an ideal island state; the capital is hidden by sentence position

explanation.surface: Someone wants us to think this spot is ideal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' at the start looks like 'additionally', but it is Thomas More, the Tudor author.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More coined the name for his imaginary island with an ideal society, now any ideal state.

clue.text: One very impressed by sensual and riotous feasting

indicators.note: impressed means pressed into, so the two letters are set inside the sensual word

parts.note: carnal means sensual or fleshly
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone very taken with sensual, wild revelry.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnival is a period of public merrymaking and feasting, as before Lent.

clue.text: Special gift, article left in shelter

indicators.note: in places the two letters inside the shelter word

parts.note: a tent is a shelter
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A unique present, an item abandoned in a hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent is a natural aptitude or flair, a gift in that sense.

clue.text: A very powerful man, he controls boxing clubs

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing in a box, so the controls word encloses the card-suit letter

parts.note: rules means controls
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A strongman who runs boxing clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing clubs' looks like gyms for boxers, but 'boxing' means enclosing C (clubs) inside RULES.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercules, the hero of classical myth famed for his twelve labours, stands for any man of great strength.
